PROJECT REPORT: Automated Scoliosis Detection & Recommendation System
1. Abstract
Scoliosis is a medical condition defined by an abnormal lateral curvature of the spine. Early detection is crucial for effective treatment, yet traditional screening methods often require frequent X-rays and manual measurement by specialists, which can be time-consuming and prone to human error. This project proposes an automated web-based system for Scoliosis detection using Computer Vision and Image Processing techniques.
The system utilizes the Hough Transform algorithm to identify spinal curvature from X-ray images and calculates the Cobb Angle to classify the severity of the condition (Normal, Mild, Moderate, Severe). Furthermore, it integrates a rule-based Expert System to provide personalized exercise recommendations and medical advice. The application features a secure database for patient history tracking and a doctor's dashboard, providing a complete, low-cost digital health solution.
2. System Architecture
The project follows a Client-Server Architecture. The client (browser) handles image acquisition, while the server (Python) processes the image using OpenCV and manages the SQLite database.
2.1. Architecture Components
 * Presentation Layer (Frontend):
   * HTML5/CSS3: Provides the user interface for image upload and result visualization.
   * Responsive Design: Ensures the tool works on desktops and tablets.
 * Application Layer (Backend):
   * Python HTTP Server: Handles HTTP requests without heavy frameworks, demonstrating low-level socket programming.
   * OpenCV Module: Performs the core image processing (Grayscale, Edge Detection, Line Mapping).
   * Logic Engine: Calculates the geometric angle and maps it to health advice.
 * Data Layer (Database):
   * SQLite: Stores patient records, image paths, calculated angles, and timestamps.
3. Modules Description
Module 1: Image Pre-processing
Before analysis, raw X-ray images often contain noise that can confuse the algorithm.
 * Grayscale Conversion: Converts the 3-channel (RGB) image to a single-channel (Gray) image to reduce computational complexity.
 * Gaussian Blurring: A smoothing filter (5x5 kernel) is applied to remove "salt-and-pepper" noise, ensuring that only significant edges are detected.
Module 2: Feature Extraction (The "AI" Core)
This module identifies the vertebrae structure.
 * Canny Edge Detection: Computes the gradient intensity of the image to find the boundaries of the bones.
   * Thresholds: Low (50), High (150).
 * Hough Line Transform: A feature extraction technique used to detect straight lines. The probabilistic version (HoughLinesP) is used to identify the two most dominant lines representing the spinal tilt.
Module 3: Geometric Analysis (Cobb Angle Calculation)
The system calculates the angle between the two dominant lines found in Module 2.
 * Formula: The angle \theta of a line is calculated using \arctan(\frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}).
 * Result: The absolute difference between the angles of the top and bottom lines gives the simulated Cobb Angle.
Module 4: Expert System & Database
 * Classification: The calculated angle is categorized:
   * < 10°: Normal
   * 10° - 25°: Mild
   * 25° - 45°: Moderate
   * > 45°: Severe
     > 
 * Recommendation Engine: Returns specific exercises (e.g., Plank, Bird-Dog) based on the category.
 * Dashboard: Fetches historical data from scoliosis.db for the admin view.
4. Technologies Used
| Component | Technology | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| Language | Python 3.x | Extensive support for scientific computing. |
| Image Library | OpenCV (cv2) | Industry standard for Computer Vision. |
| Math Library | NumPy | Efficient array handling for geometric calculations. |
| Web Server | http.server | Lightweight, built-in Python library (No frameworks). |
| Database | SQLite3 | Serverless, zero-configuration database. |
| Frontend | HTML5, CSS3 | Universal browser compatibility. |
5. Installation & User Manual
5.1. Hardware Requirements
 * Processor: Intel Core i3 or higher (or equivalent AMD).
 * RAM: 4GB minimum.
 * Storage: 500MB free space.
5.2. Software Requirements
 * OS: Windows 10/11, Linux, or macOS.
 * Python: Version 3.8 or higher.
 * Browser: Chrome, Firefox, or Edge.
5.3. Setup Instructions
 * Install Python: Download from python.org.
 * Install Libraries: Open terminal and run:
   pip install opencv-python numpy

 * Run the Server:
   cd scoliosis_project
python server.py

 * Access Application: Open http://localhost:8000 in your web browser.
6. Future Scope
While the current system uses geometric analysis, future iterations could include:
 * Deep Learning (U-Net): Training a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to segment individual vertebrae for higher accuracy than line detection.
 * Cloud Integration: Hosting the database on AWS/Firebase for remote doctor access.
 * Real-time Video: Analyzing posture in real-time using a webcam (Video feed processing).
7. Conclusion
The "Automated Scoliosis Detection System" successfully demonstrates the application of Computer Vision in healthcare.
